c.tagline: A Tibetan-plateau town of golden monasteries, grasslands and the gateway to the eastern Himalaya.

taxi.fareNote: Didi is the easiest way to book a car; metered street taxis are cheap but drivers often prefer a flat rate to the monastery, Napahai or the airport. The Dukezong Old Town lanes are pedestrian, so cars drop you at the gates.

emergency.note: 110 is police, 120 the ambulance and 119 fire. At 3,200 m altitude take it easy on arrival - clinics stock oxygen for altitude sickness. English is rarely spoken, so a translation app or written Chinese address helps.

avoid.reason: Altitude sickness is the main risk on arrival; be wary of hard-sell 'Tibetan medicine' and gallery stops on tours.

hood_desc: The 1,300-year-old Tibetan old town on Guishan Hill, a warren of cobbled lanes, timber Tibetan houses, cafes and guesthouses crowned by the giant golden prayer wheel; atmospheric and walkable, the most characterful base despite a 2014 fire and its careful rebuild.

Modern Shangri-La spreading below the old town, with the bus station, hospitals, supermarkets, chain hotels and everyday services; the practical, convenient base for transport and for acclimatising to the altitude before heading out.

The area about five kilometres north around Ganden Sumtseling, Yunnan's largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery (a 'little Potala'), overlooking the mirror-like Lamu Yangcuo lake; a serene, sights-focused base among monasteries and meadows.

The seasonal grassland lake about eight kilometres northwest, a Ramsar wetland and black-necked-crane haven ringed by pastures and Tibetan villages; a scenic, quiet base for wide-open highland landscapes and horseback rides.

A pastoral valley about twenty kilometres south along the G214 toward Lijiang, famed for autumn colours, barley fields and 'ten-thousand-flower' meadows; a tranquil rural base close to Napa and the road out.
lodging: Arro Khampa by Zinc Journey Shangri-La

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water; the 3,200 m altitude makes hydration important.

transit.pay: Pay city buses in exact-change cash or, more commonly, by scanning Alipay or WeChat Pay; foreign visitors should set up mobile pay in advance, as cash and cards are increasingly awkward. Taxis and Didi are paid the same way.
transit.hours: City buses run roughly 7am-8pm; after that use Didi or a taxi. Many outlying sights are best reached by chartered car.
transit.note: Shangri-La has no metro or rail transit; getting around means a handful of city bus lines, Didi and taxis, plus walking the pedestrian old town. Sights are spread across the plateau, so most visitors charter a car or join a tour for Songzanlin, Napahai and Pudacuo.

train: Lijiang-Shangri-La railway (opened November 2023) with trains to Lijiang, Dali and Kunming
bus: Intercity coaches to Lijiang, Dali, Kunming and Deqin (Meili Snow Mountain)

transit.m: Airport shuttle bus to downtown Shangri-La (~20 min)
Taxi or Didi to the old town (~15 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in mainland China and is generally not expected in restaurants, taxis or hotels; a small tip for a private trekking guide or driver is at your discretion.

food.name: Yak Meat Hotpot
food.desc: The high-altitude centrepiece: yak beef and bones simmered in a milky bone broth with wild mushrooms, potatoes and greens, eaten around a shared pot.

places.name: Yintong Yak Hotpot
places.note: Old-town specialist known for tender, chewy local yak and a clean bone broth.

places.name: Kangba Herdsman Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Big Khampa-style dining room doing yak hotpot with butter lamps and song performances.

places.name: Niu Niu Cafe
places.note: Set meals pairing yak hotpot with garlic mushrooms and stir-fried greens; easy for solo diners.

food.name: Tibetan Momo
food.desc: Hand-pleated dumplings steamed or pan-fried, filled with minced yak, mutton or potato and cheese, served with chilli-and-vinegar dip.

places.name: Shunshun Snacks
places.note: Easy-to-find snack house in the old town doing momo, noodles and Tibetan small plates.

places.name: The Silent Holy Stones
places.note: Tibetan-run restaurant with modest decor, generous portions and very fair prices.

places.name: Jingjing Mani Stone Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Family kitchen serving momo alongside yak ribs and barley staples.

food.name: Tsampa
food.desc: Roasted highland barley flour kneaded by hand with butter tea into a dense dough. The everyday fuel of the Tibetan plateau, filling and nutty.

places.name: Kangba Herdsman Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Will show you how to knead tsampa properly with butter tea at the table.

places.name: Minzhu Lamu Shangri-La Kitchen
places.note: Home-style Tibetan cooking with tsampa, barley cakes and yak butter on the menu.

places.name: Dukezong old town morning market
places.note: Buy roasted barley flour by weight from local vendors and try it the way herders do.

food.name: Yak Yoghurt
food.desc: Thick, tart set yoghurt from yak milk, served in a bowl with a spoon of honey or sugar. Far richer and sharper than cow-milk yoghurt.

places.name: Well 3294
places.note: Quaint old-town cafe pouring yak yoghurt in several flavours, almost everything under 20 yuan.

places.name: Niu Niu Cafe
places.note: Reliable stop for yak yoghurt and sweet tea between old-town wandering.

places.name: Dukezong old town market stalls
places.note: Local dairy vendors sell yak yoghurt in plain plastic tubs for a fraction of cafe prices.

food.name: Matsutake Mushrooms
food.desc: Diqing is one of the world's great matsutake regions. In season (June to September) they arrive sliced raw, grilled on butter or dropped into chicken soup.

places.name: Gu Bo Lang
places.note: Yunnan-Tibetan restaurant that plates wild mushrooms well when matsutake is in season.

places.name: Kangba Herdsman Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Adds matsutake to hotpot and chicken soup through the summer mushroom season.

places.name: Shangri-La wild mushroom market
places.note: Seasonal trading market where matsutake and other wild fungi are sold fresh each morning.

food.name: Pipa Pork and Air-Dried Yak
food.desc: Highland preserving at work: whole pork flattened and salt-cured into a lute shape, plus strips of yak air-dried in the thin mountain wind.

places.name: Minzhu Lamu Shangri-La Kitchen
places.note: Serves cured pipa pork and dried yak the way local families eat them.

places.name: The Silent Holy Stones
places.note: Tibetan-run kitchen with air-dried yak among the cold starters.

places.name: Dukezong old town market stalls
places.note: Cured meat vendors sell dried yak strips by the bag; good trekking snack.

food.name: Yak Butter Tea (Su You Cha)
food.desc: Brick tea churned with yak butter and salt into a warm, savoury, broth-like drink. An acquired taste, and genuinely useful against the altitude.

places.name: Kangba Herdsman Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Churned fresh and refilled endlessly; the classic full-ceremony experience.

places.name: Well 3294
places.note: Gentle place to try butter tea, with sweet milk tea as a fallback if it is too savoury.

places.name: The Silent Holy Stones
places.note: Warm local hosts happy to explain the etiquette of drinking and refilling the bowl.

food.name: Qingke Jiu (highland barley wine)
food.desc: Home-brewed barley liquor, cloudy and mildly sweet in the low-strength version, fiery when distilled. Go slow; altitude amplifies it.

places.name: Kangba Herdsman Tibetan Restaurant
places.note: Barley wine poured with the meal and the traditional three-sip, three-refill toast.

places.name: Gu Bo Lang
places.note: Stocks both the mild homebrew style and stronger distilled barley spirit.

places.name: Dukezong old town shops
places.note: Small shops around the square sell bottled qingke jiu to take away.

landmarks: Ganden Sumtseling Monastery (Songzanlin)
Yunnan's largest Tibetan Buddhist monastery, a 17th-century hillside complex of gilded roofs and whitewashed walls often called the little Potala Palace.
Dukezong Ancient Town
A 1,300-year-old Tibetan old town of cobbled lanes and timber houses, lovingly rebuilt after the 2014 fire and glowing with lantern-lit charm.
Guishan Park Giant Prayer Wheel
The world's largest prayer wheel, a 21-metre golden cylinder crowning Turtle Hill that visitors join hands to spin above Dukezong's rooftops.
Napa Lake (Napahai)
A vast seasonal wetland ringed by mountains where black-necked cranes winter and Tibetan horses graze golden grasslands in autumn.
Baiji Temple (Hundred Chickens Temple)
A small hilltop temple wandered by free-roaming chickens, rewarding the short climb with prayer-flag panoramas over Shangri-La's old town.
Shika Snow Mountain
A 4,500-metre sacred peak reached by cable car, offering alpine meadows, azalea slopes and, on clear days, views to Meili Snow Mountain.
Dabao Temple (Dabaosi)
One of the region's oldest temple sites, an atmospheric complex amid grasslands considered a cradle of Tibetan Buddhism in Yunnan.
Ringha Monastery
A 300-year-old Tibetan monastery complex four kilometres north of Dukezong old town, its whitewashed prayer halls climbing a pine-covered hillside above the valley.
Gucheng Zangjingtang
A former Red Army memorial hall turned scripture chamber on the road between the old town and Songzanlin, its wooden galleries lined with Tibetan sutras.
Zhongxin Assembly Hall
A historic Naxi-style assembly hall at the highest point of Dukezong old town, recalling the era when Shangri-La was a trading post on the Tea Horse Road.

train.note: Shangri-La has no international trains. The Lijiang-Shangri-La railway, opened in November 2023, runs south from Shangri-La station to Lijiang in about 1.25 hours and continues to Dali and Kunming; it is the fastest and most scenic way in, and has largely replaced the long bus journey up from Lijiang. Book on 12306 with your passport, and note the station is a few kilometres from the old town so you will need a taxi or the shuttle bus.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Shangri-La. Long-distance buses from the Shangri-La bus station run to Lijiang (about 4 hours), Dali (about 7 hours), Kunming (about 10-12 hours) and north to Deqin and Feilaisi for the Meili Snow Mountain viewpoints (about 4-5 hours). The Deqin road has no rail alternative, so the bus remains essential for anyone heading further into the Tibetan borderlands; buy at the counter with your passport and go early, as afternoon departures are few.

ferry.note: Shangri-La lies at about 3,200 m on the Tibetan plateau margin in northwest Yunnan, hundreds of kilometres from the sea, and the nearby Jinsha river is unnavigable - there are no passenger ferry services.

half.name: Napahai Lake
half.blurb: A seasonal grassland lake ~8 km northwest, a Ramsar wetland wintering black-necked cranes, with horse riding across the surrounding pastures.

half.name: Dukezong Old Town & Great Prayer Wheel
half.blurb: The rebuilt Tibetan old town with the world's largest prayer wheel on Guishan Hill, best at dusk when locals turn it together.

full.name: Pudacuo National Park
full.blurb: China's first national park ~22 km east, with the alpine lakes Shudu and Bita, boardwalks, meadows and fir forest above 3,500 m.

full.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge
full.blurb: One of the world's deepest river canyons ~2-3 hr south toward Lijiang, where the upper Yangtze roars between 5,000 m peaks on a classic high-trail trek.

full.name: Balagezong Grand Canyon
full.blurb: A dramatic canyon-and-sacred-mountain scenic area ~2.5 hr northwest, with glass walkways, a cliffside Tibetan village and the region's highest peak.
